 Typhoon to turn away from Taiwan; heavy rain still forecast
 Staff writer, with CNA 
 Add TT as Preferred Source 
 Typhoon Champi is forecast to turn northward earlier than previously expected, sparing Taiwan a direct hit but still bringing heavy rain to the north of the country on Friday and Saturday, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) said yesterday.
 Typhoon Champi had strengthened and increased in size over the past 12 hours, and as of yesterday afternoon, was packing sustained winds of 198kph near its center, CWA forecaster Cheng Chieh-jen (鄭傑仁) said.
 However, due to the weakening of a Pacific high-pressure system the storm is now expected to turn northward earlier than initially forecast, likely around Japan’s Ishigaki Island, Cheng said.
 A satellite image shows Typhoon Champi southeast of Taiwan at 9pm yesterday. 
 Photo: The Central Weather Administration
 As Champi brushes past northeastern Taiwan, it is expected to be a strong "moderate" typhoon or weak "intense" typhoon per the CWA’s classification system, which defines the latter as having sustained winds of more than 184kph, he said.
 The CWA could issue a sea warning tomorrow night or Thursday at the earliest, and a land warning on Thursday evening or Friday, he said.
 The warning would likely apply to northern and eastern Taiwan, with the north and Yilan County, in particular, facing possible heavy or extremely heavy rain on Friday and Saturday, he added.
 As the typhoon approaches on Thursday, there would continue to be scattered rain showers in Yilan and northern Taiwan, Cheng said, adding that those areas could report heavy or extremely heavy rain on Friday and Saturday, while scattered showers are forecast for other regions.
 As Typhoon Champi weakens and moves away from Taiwan on Sunday, cloudy to clear weather conditions would prevail in most regions, with the exception of lingering showers in the east and on the Hengchun Peninsula (恆春半島) in the south, Cheng said.

 Donated vessel will not patrol waters near Taiwan: premier
 2026-10-21 
 A patrol vessel donated by the Coast Guard Administration (CGA) to the Philippines would not be used in waters near Taiwan or areas where Taiwanese fishing vessels operate, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) said yesterday.
The vessel, formerly the CGA's 500-tonne-class Kinmen (金門), was commissioned into the Philippine Coast Guard on Oct. 2.
Speaking at the Legislative Yuan, Cho said the Philippines had pledged during the donation process that the vessel would be used only for designated missions and would not operate in waters related to Taiwan. 
The vessel could even provide assistance to Taiwan if needed, he added.
